newsitems.title: Neat! Release Date & Full Game Details
newsitems.author: Molly
newsitems.contents: Hey everyone!First of all, thank you so much for all the wishlists and for playing the demo! Neat! reached over 25k wishlists, and we're incredibly happy to see so many people excited for Neat! Reading your comments kept us going through the final stretch of development. Your feedback truly shaped the game.Release Date: September 14We're happy to announce that Neat! will be releasing on September 14!We can't wait to see you step into Molly's shoes, meet all of her clients, and untangle every mess.Full GameHere's what's coming in the full version:8 hand-crafted locations, each with its own client and its own story told through objects:A grandmother's garden, where Molly's tidying service beginsA neighborhood library after a "chamber music evening" that ended as a rock concertA VTuber's streaming room, hours before her first live showA living room the owner swears is hauntedA hikikomori room, he genuinely has everything he'll ever needA single mom's kitchenA Japanese konbini on the night shiftAnd one last space we won't spoil, the most personal one of allSee You on September 14Thank you again for all the support, feedback, and wishlists.

newsitems.title: Demo Patch #2
newsitems.author: Molly
newsitems.contents: Thank you so much for being with us during Steam Next Fest, and thank you for all your feedback — it means the world to us.We have a lot of ideas and plans for improvements, and today we're releasing new patch we've been working on over the past week.What's new:Safe Zone added — you can now freely drop items in the area outside the room when there's no place to put them. This helps avoid soft-locks when you're holding an item and can't place it anywhere.Improved sorting order for items — overlapping bugs and visual glitches should now be greatly reduced.Interaction zone icons — doors and interactive items now show icons for their interaction zones, so you can be sure an item won't block a door when you place it.Resolution settings — you can now change your resolution preferences.Localization fixes.Plus lots of other small fixes and improvements.Thank you again for your support! See you in the next update!

newsitems.title: Bug fixes - version 0.42
newsitems.author: Molly
newsitems.contents: Fixes:Bug with item placement (Konbini)Bug with magazines previewVisual bug with vertical item placement (Kitchen)Visual bug with sugar and coffee standAdded stacking for frozen vegetablesMinor localization fixes

newsitems.title: Demo Patch #1
newsitems.author: Molly
newsitems.contents: It's been a week since demo release, and over 1,000 players have tried Neat!Thank you all for the feedback and support. We plan to update the demo continuously up until release, so expect more patches on the way.Today's patch focuses on quality-of-life improvements, bug fixes, and a partly new UI.More stacking! We heard you love stacking items, so we added more ways to do it. If you feel like something should stack but doesn't — let us know.New UI for quests and dialogues. This is the first step toward a fully refreshed UI.Fixed the language selector. Last patch we accidentally broke localization, and some of you couldn't select your preferred language. That's fixed now — sorry about that!Less chaos at the start. We heard the levels could feel overwhelming, so we've rebalanced things slightly and added more items to the starting boxes. Let us know how it feels now.Thanks for playing, and keep the feedback coming! 💛

newsitems.title: The Neat Demo is Live — See You at Steam Next Fest!
newsitems.author: Molly
newsitems.contents: Huge thanks to all the playtesters who reported bugs and pointed out what worked and what didn't. Your feedback shaped this demo, and we couldn't have shipped it without you.We're already preparing one more patch before the festival, landing in the coming days — focused on bug fixes, a UI update, and a handful of other improvements.Thank you for joining us on this journey and for all the kind words along the way. We truly appreciate every bit of your feedback and support. 💛

newsitems.title: Tooltips, Gamepad Support, New Quests & More
newsitems.author: Molly
newsitems.contents: Hey everyone! We've been heads-down working on some big changes, and here's what's new:Tooltips & Tags Hover over any item and you'll now see its name and a set of tags that hint at where it might belong. Think of them as gentle nudges — not rules, just ideas. We'll be expanding the tag set over time.Gamepad & Steam Deck Support You can now play Neat with a controller. Steam Deck players, this one's for you.Quests Rethought Quests no longer tell you exactly where to put something. You decide. The goal is still to tidy up — how you do it is up to you. Old quests have been updated to match this new philosophy.Skip Tutorial Option For our most dedicated playtesters who've been with us since the beginning — you can now skip the tutorial. You've earned it.New Items Fresh items added to the kitchen and konbini, including ice cream.A note on the shop and inventoryWe're removing them. They were fun to build and fun to play with, but right now we want to focus our energy on the parts of Neat that feel the most satisfying. The shop and inventory aren't gone forever — we just need to be honest about where our attention should be. Thanks for understanding.As always, leave feedback in the discussions. Every playtest helps.Share feedback: Discord

newsitems.title: New Playtest Level — Konbini 6-7
newsitems.author: Molly
newsitems.contents: A new level is in the playtest build: a Japanese konbini at five in the morning.Yuki, a university student on the night shift, fell asleep mid-study session. The delivery boxes are still sealed. The coffee station is in pieces. Nothing is on the shelves. The store opens in an hour, and if the manager sees it like this, Yuki is finished.Don't forget to drop you comments and feedback!Discord

newsitems.title: Neat Playtest Patch #1 — Doors 🚪
newsitems.author: Molly
newsitems.contents: Just a week ago we launched the playtest, and since then we’ve received tons of feedback, bug reports, suggestions, and just kind words — thank you, seriously.We’re pushing regular updates to improve the experience and address your feedback as fast as possible.Today’s update is all about Doors — easily the most discussed feature this week. So we went deep on fixing and improving them. If something still feels off — tell us.DoorsDoors now won’t open if something is blocking them → The door and blocking object will highlight in red → Just move the item to unblock itAdded proper sliding animations for boxes → If it should slide, it now actually slidesImproved open/close interaction triggers → It should now feel much clearer when you’re interacting with a doorUpdated cursor highlighting → Easier to understand what’s interactiveOther FixesCutlery Organizer → Reduced pixel hunting when placing items → Still too tricky? Let us know — we’re tuning itAdded more localizationsUpdated win notification → No longer interrupts cleaning → Clearer indication that the level is completeLots of small fixes and improvementsArt / What’s NextNew level coming soon: Konbini → We’re already working on it → Would love your ideas — what items should be there?

newsitems.title: Neat Playtest is Live
newsitems.author: moopunkgames
newsitems.contents: The Neat playtest is live.After months of heads-down work, we're opening the doors. Starting today, you can play Neat.How to joinHead to the Neat Steam page and hit the green "Request Access" button on the playtest widget. We're approving requests in waves throughout the day — if you don't see an invite immediately, hang tight. You'll get one. Already in? Just launch from your library.What's in this buildThe first level: the Kitchen. More levels are on the way in future updates — this build is where we find out what's working before we build out the rest of the world.We want your feedback — especially the uncomfortable kindWhere to send itBug reports and general feedback: Discord (Join right now to apply special role)Clips and screenshots: post them anywhere, tag us, we'll see themHow long it runsThe playtest is open through end of May. We'll ship the updates on what we're hearing from you.Thank you
